reviews.reasoning: Re-derived the seam from both witnesses rather than the row's assertions. Ps 30 is a shift+1 psalm (ps_lib.web_to_mt), so the title dual-cite web:Ps.30.0 = oshb:Ps.30.1 is arithmetically correct, and the genre labels the device_notes names are present in the byte-true title verse oshb:Ps.30.1 (מִזְמ֡וֹר שִׁיר חֲנֻכַּ֖ת הַבַּ֣יִת), which carries mizmor, shir and the dedication note alongside le-David. The closing warrant also holds: זַמְּר֣וּ with the vocative חֲסִידָ֑יו opens oshb:Ps.30.5 = web:Ps.30.4 and collates at byte tier, so the addressee shift from Yahweh-directed testimony to a congregational summons is a genuine tier-1 signal at the 30:3|30:4 seam. pmarks_Ps.json holds 0 selah verses in Ps 30, and the row makes no selah, pe/samekh or acrostic claim. The span is right and I do not contest it. The defect is disclosure: the row's span-closing verse is the one ketiv/qere verse in the whole cluster, the row quotes it in full, and nothing at any layer discloses that. check_marks.py returns GREEN here because it validates K/Q claims that are made, not K/Q disclosures that are omitted, so the omission is a reviewer-level find rather than a validator hit.

challenges.claim: The row quotes web:Ps.30.3 in full as its span-closing evidence without disclosing that the verse's MT counterpart oshb:Ps.30.4 is the sole ketiv/qere verse in Psalms 30-31 (1 of 1), and the WEB wording it quotes tracks the qere.
challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json kq inventory, filtered span-scoped over MT Ps.30.1-Ps.30.13 and Ps.31.1-Ps.31.25: 1 verse, Ps.30.4 (1 note); 0 elsewhere in either psalm (book totals 68 notes over 65 verses). Byte-true MT oshb:Ps.30.4 carries both readings adjacently: חִ֝יִּיתַ֗נִי מיורדי מִיָּֽרְדִי בֽוֹר -- the unpointed מיורדי is the ketiv, the pointed מִיָּֽרְדִי the qere. Dual-cite arithmetic: web 30:3 + 1 = oshb 30:4 (Ps 30 is shift+1). The row's curly-quoted English is “Yahweh, you have brought up my soul from Sheol. You have kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit.” (web:Ps.30.3); the singular “I should not go down” tracks the qere's singular rather than the ketiv's plural participle. I select no reading -- the zone is held -- but the row leans its seam on a verse it quotes without the mandated K/Q disclosure: rationale, observed_substrate_signals and device_notes carry 0 K/Q disclosures between them.

reviews.reasoning: Both seams re-derived from bytes and both hold. Opening: oshb:Ps.30.5 = web:Ps.30.4 (shift+1) reads זַמְּר֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חֲסִידָ֑יו, collating at byte tier -- a plural imperative plus the vocative חֲסִידָ֑יו, a tier-1 addressee shift away from the direct address to Yahweh that runs through web:Ps.30.3. Closing: oshb:Ps.30.7 = web:Ps.30.6 opens וַ֭אֲנִי אָמַ֣רְתִּי (byte tier), returning the psalmist's own voice, so the maxim of web:Ps.30.5 is correctly bounded on both sides. Arithmetic checked against the offset map at every cite; the single boundary ref web:Ps.30.6 mirrors the only out-of-span verse argued. pmarks_Ps.json: 0 selah verses in Ps 30 and no K/Q in MT Ps.30.5-Ps.30.6, so no disclosure obligation arises inside this span. Two observations that do not reach defect level. First, the device_notes calls the antithesis night-to-morning, following WEB's “Weeping may stay for the night” (web:Ps.30.5), whereas byte-true MT oshb:Ps.30.6 reads בָּ֭עֶרֶב (evening); the antithesis is present in both witnesses, so the seam is untouched, but the phrasing leans on the English. Second, this row's opening verse is where the psalm's real closing lexical frame originates: skeleton sweep זמר returns 41 verses book-wide and exactly 2 in Ps 30 -- oshb:Ps.30.5 = web:Ps.30.4 and oshb:Ps.30.13 = web:Ps.30.12 -- and the two ydh spellings land the same way (הודו: 15 verses book-wide, 1 in Ps 30 at oshb:Ps.30.5; אודך: 14 verses book-wide, 1 in Ps 30 at oshb:Ps.30.13). That frame spans the psalm rather than binding web:Ps.30.5 to web:Ps.30.6, so it does not argue against this seam; the disclosure obligation falls on the row that asserts an inclusio, where I have filed it.

The span itself survives re-derivation. The opening warrant וַ֭אֲנִי אָמַ֣רְתִּי at oshb:Ps.30.7 = web:Ps.30.6 collates at byte tier, the resolution verb הָפַ֣כְתָּ at oshb:Ps.30.12 = web:Ps.30.11 likewise, both dual-cites are arithmetically correct for a shift+1 psalm, and the row correctly runs to the psalm's end without crossing a psalm boundary. The embedded-quotation observation is honest about its basis (it names the WEB's own punctuation), which is the right way to lean on a single-witness rendering feature. What fails is the device_notes inclusio, and it fails lexically in both witnesses, not on taste. The correction also moves the device's other end into a different row, so the cure is a seam-pair edit authored once and installed on both rows in the same pass.

challenges.claim: The device_notes inclusio is false: the psalm's closing verse does not echo the extolling verb of web:Ps.30.1, and its actual verbal echoes bind it to web:Ps.30.4, which lies outside this row.
challenges.evidence: Skeleton sweep רומ: 24 verses book-wide, 1 verse in Ps 30 -- oshb:Ps.30.2 = web:Ps.30.1. Spelling sweep ארוממך: 3 verses book-wide, the same 1 verse in Ps 30. Neither returns oshb:Ps.30.13 = web:Ps.30.12. Byte-true MT: oshb:Ps.30.2 opens אֲרוֹמִמְךָ֣; oshb:Ps.30.13 reads לְמַ֤עַן יְזַמֶּרְךָ֣ כָ֭בוֹד וְלֹ֣א יִדֹּ֑ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י לְעוֹלָ֥ם אוֹדֶֽךָּ -- its verbs are יְזַמֶּרְךָ֣ and אוֹדֶֽךָּ, not the root of אֲרוֹמִמְךָ֣. The repetition that does exist runs to web:Ps.30.4: skeleton sweep זמר returns 41 verses book-wide and exactly 2 in Ps 30, oshb:Ps.30.5 = web:Ps.30.4 (זַמְּר֣וּ) and oshb:Ps.30.13 = web:Ps.30.12 (יְזַמֶּרְךָ֣); the ydh spellings pair the same two verses (הודו, 15 verses book-wide, 1 in Ps 30 at oshb:Ps.30.5 = וְ֝הוֹד֗וּ; אודך, 14 verses book-wide, 1 in Ps 30 at oshb:Ps.30.13 = אוֹדֶֽךָּ). WEB agrees on the surface: “I will extol you, Yahweh” (web:Ps.30.1) is not echoed at “to the end that my heart may sing praise to you, and not be silent. Yahweh my God, I will give thanks to you forever!” (web:Ps.30.12), whereas “Sing praise to Yahweh, you saints of his. Give thanks to his holy name.” (web:Ps.30.4) supplies both verbs. The frame therefore terminates in this row and originates in the row holding web:Ps.30.4, and web:Ps.30.4 is not in this row's boundary_evidence_refs.

reviews.reasoning: Every Hebrew run in this row collates at byte tier, which is quotation-grade, and the title evidence is handled correctly: web:Ps.31.0 = oshb:Ps.31.1 is the owner-ruled form for a shift+1 psalm, and byte-true oshb:Ps.31.1 (לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד) does carry the lamnatseach, mizmor and le-David labels the device_notes names. pmarks_Ps.json shows 0 selah and 0 K/Q verses in Ps 31, so no disclosure obligation arises anywhere in this span. I am not contesting the span: the refuge plea and the deliverance testimony do cohere from web:Ps.31.1 to web:Ps.31.8. What I contest is the evidence, and the central item is that the row's only stated ground for rejecting the rival break is an absence claim that its own hinge verse falsifies -- the row quotes the first 3 words of oshb:Ps.31.6 and stops exactly where the counterevidence begins. That matters more than usual because this row carries confidence high, and once the rival-rejection warrant fails, the calibration is not supported by what remains.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative's warrant -- that no vocative renewal interrupts the strophe until web:Ps.31.9 -- is falsified inside the row's own span at web:Ps.31.5 = oshb:Ps.31.6, the verse the row cites as its hinge.
challenges.evidence: Byte-true MT oshb:Ps.31.6 in full (8 words): בְּיָדְךָ֮ אַפְקִ֪יד ר֫וּחִ֥י פָּדִ֖יתָה אוֹתִ֥י יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֣ל אֱמֶֽת. The row quotes the first 3, בְּיָדְךָ֮ אַפְקִ֪יד ר֫וּחִ֥י; the verse continues פָּדִ֖יתָה אוֹתִ֥י יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֣ל אֱמֶֽת. פָּדִ֖יתָה is second-person singular, so יְהוָ֗ה cannot be its subject and stands as address. Both witnesses render it that way: WEB sets the name off between commas -- “Into your hand I commend my spirit. You redeem me, Yahweh, God of truth.” (web:Ps.31.5). Dual-cite arithmetic: web 31:5 + 1 = oshb 31:6 (Ps 31 is shift+1). The staged extract exposes 3 fields per MT verse (text, language, web) and no morphology layer, so this is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, which is the method the toolkit prescribes. check_universals.py flags the not/until form, which carries 0 digit-bearing sweeps in its field. For completeness the divine name occurs in 3 verses of the span (skeleton sweep יהוה: oshb:Ps.31.2 = web:Ps.31.1, oshb:Ps.31.6 = web:Ps.31.5, oshb:Ps.31.7 = web:Ps.31.6), of which the first two are address and the third (וַ֝אֲנִ֗י אֶל יְהוָ֥ה בָּטָֽחְתִּי) is prepositional, so the absence claim fails on exactly one verse -- but that one verse is the row's own hinge.

challenges.claim: The curly-quoted English attributed to web:Ps.31.2-3 reproduces exactly 1 WEB verse, web:Ps.31.2, and the Hebrew it is paired with maps to that same 1 verse, so the range end web:Ps.31.3 is carried by 0 of the 2 members of the pair.
challenges.evidence: The Hebrew run collates at byte tier as the COMPLETE MT verse oshb:Ps.31.3, all 12 words (הַטֵּ֤ה אֵלַ֨י אָזְנְךָ֮ מְהֵרָ֪ה הַצִּ֫ילֵ֥נִי הֱיֵ֤ה לִ֨י לְֽצוּר מָ֭עוֹז לְבֵ֥ית מְצוּד֗וֹת לְהוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי), and ps_lib.mt_to_web(31, 3) returns web:Ps.31.2. The quoted English “Bow down your ear to me. Deliver me speedily. Be to me a strong rock, a house of defense to save me.” is web:Ps.31.2 in full and nothing more; web:Ps.31.3 reads “For you are my rock and my fortress, therefore for your name’s sake lead me and guide me.” and appears in neither the Hebrew nor the gloss. The pair as printed displays a one-MT-verse-to-two-WEB-verse mapping that the offset map does not license for a shift+1 psalm; the cure is to cite the quote at web:Ps.31.2 and, if the imperative cluster really is meant to run through web:Ps.31.3 = oshb:Ps.31.4, to quote that verse's imperatives too rather than widen the ref under the existing quote.

reviews.reasoning: The opening seam is well made and I do not contest it: חָנֵּ֥נִי יְהוָה֮ at oshb:Ps.31.10 = web:Ps.31.9 collates at byte tier and is an imperative-plus-vocative petition restarting direct address after the declarative testimony of web:Ps.31.7-Ps.31.8, which is a tier-1 discourse-frame signal, and the dual-cite arithmetic in this row is correct at every ref. The closing end is where it breaks. Both the rationale and the second substrate signal name oshb:Ps.31.13 = web:Ps.31.12 as the verse that closes the strophe, but the span runs one verse further. The row therefore never argues the verse its own seam turns on, and the verse it does argue carries a different image from the one the seam needs. I read this as a numbering slip rather than a judgement call, because the MT number the row settles on is the same integer as the span's WEB end -- the classic shift+1 trap in this book -- and the row's other cites are correct. Secondary, not filed: the device_notes absence claim carries no digit (check_universals flags it), though it is accurate on the natural reading, since pmarks_Ps.json holds 0 selah verses in Ps 31 and psalm_device_inventory.json puts no acrostic or doxology in this psalm; paseq segs do fall at MT Ps.31.12 and Ps.31.14, but paseq is seg layer rather than a psalm-level device, so the claim stands as written.

challenges.claim: The row twice identifies oshb:Ps.31.13 = web:Ps.31.12 as the verse closing the strophe, but the span closes 1 verse later at web:Ps.31.13 = oshb:Ps.31.14, a verse left unargued in 3 of the row's 3 prose layers.
challenges.evidence: Span is Ps.31.9-Ps.31.13 in WEB numbering and ps_lib.web_to_mt(31, 13) returns (31, 14), so the final verse of the span is oshb:Ps.31.14, byte-true כִּ֤י שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי דִּבַּ֥ת רַבִּים֮ מָג֪וֹר מִסָּ֫בִ֥יב בְּהִוָּסְדָ֣ם יַ֣חַד עָלַ֑י לָקַ֖חַת נַפְשִׁ֣י זָמָֽמוּ -- WEB “For I have heard the slander of many, terror on every side, while they conspire together against me, they plot to take away my life.” (web:Ps.31.13). That is a slander-and-conspiracy verse, not the isolation image the row says completes the span, and it is the verse the seam at web:Ps.31.13|31.14 actually turns on. The verse the row does nominate is oshb:Ps.31.13 = web:Ps.31.12, byte-true נִ֭שְׁכַּחְתִּי כְּמֵ֣ת מִלֵּ֑ב, WEB “I am forgotten from their hearts like a dead man.” (web:Ps.31.12) -- in span, correctly dual-cited, but not the close. Note the coincidence that drives it: the MT number the row treats as the close (31.13) is the same integer as the span's WEB end (31.13), while the true correspondence is web 31:13 + 1 = oshb 31:14. The span may well be right; the evidence for its closing seam is missing.

reviews.reasoning: The span is sound and I say so explicitly, because the challenge below is about warrant quality, not placement. Both quoted runs collate at byte tier and both dual-cites are arithmetically right for a shift+1 psalm: וַאֲנִ֤י עָלֶ֣יךָ בָטַ֣חְתִּי יְהוָ֑ה at oshb:Ps.31.15 = web:Ps.31.14 opens, שִׂפְתֵ֫י שָׁ֥קֶר at oshb:Ps.31.19 = web:Ps.31.18 closes, and unlike the preceding row this one lands its closing quote on the actual final verse of its span. The device_notes selah absence claim is span-scoped and correct -- pmarks_Ps.json holds 0 selah verses in Ps 31 -- and the row is right that the pivot is syntactic rather than marks-layer, which is the honest way to put it in a book with no pe/samekh layer at all. What I contest is that the pronoun-fronting description the row offers as the seam driver fits another verse in the same psalm just as well, one that sits mid-strophe inside the adjacent row with no seam, and the row does not disclose it or narrow the warrant to exclude it.

challenges.claim: The pronoun-fronting warrant offered for the seam is non-discriminating within Psalm 31 and the recurrence is undisclosed.
challenges.evidence: Skeleton sweep ואני: 31 verses book-wide, 3 verses in Ps 31 -- oshb:Ps.31.7 = web:Ps.31.6, oshb:Ps.31.15 = web:Ps.31.14, oshb:Ps.31.23 = web:Ps.31.22. The row's stated description is that the form fronts the independent pronoun against the preceding third-person image, marking the adversative turn. Byte-true oshb:Ps.31.7 fits that description at all 3 of its points, and with the same verb root as the seam verse: שָׂנֵ֗אתִי הַשֹּׁמְרִ֥ים הַבְלֵי שָׁ֑וְא וַ֝אֲנִ֗י אֶל יְהוָ֥ה בָּטָֽחְתִּי -- a third-person image (הַשֹּׁמְרִ֥ים הַבְלֵי שָׁ֑וְא) followed by fronted וַ֝אֲנִ֗י plus בָּטָֽחְתִּי, rendered by WEB as “I hate those who regard lying vanities, but I trust in Yahweh.” (web:Ps.31.6). The seam verse oshb:Ps.31.15 reads וַאֲנִ֤י עָלֶ֣יךָ בָטַ֣חְתִּי יְהוָ֑ה, the same pronoun plus the same root. oshb:Ps.31.7 sits mid-strophe in the row covering web:Ps.31.1-Ps.31.8 with 0 seams claimed at it, and the 3rd occurrence oshb:Ps.31.23 = web:Ps.31.22 is likewise interior. The seam itself is independently supported by the return of second-person address and by the byte-true close at oshb:Ps.31.19, so the span stands; the warrant needs either the disclosure or a feature that separates oshb:Ps.31.15 from oshb:Ps.31.7.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived every claim this row leans on and they all hold. Both Hebrew runs collate at byte tier: מָ֤ה רַֽב טוּבְךָ֮ at oshb:Ps.31.20 = web:Ps.31.19 and בָּר֥וּךְ יְהוָ֑ה at oshb:Ps.31.22 = web:Ps.31.21, both dual-cites correct for a shift+1 psalm. The exclamatory-particle absence claim is accurate, and the way it could have gone wrong is worth recording: skeleton sweep מה returns 193 verses book-wide and 2 in Ps 31, oshb:Ps.31.3 = web:Ps.31.2 and oshb:Ps.31.20 = web:Ps.31.19, but the first hit is מְהֵרָ֪ה (rendered 'speedily'), a different lexeme caught by contiguous consonantal substring matching, so at token level the exclamatory particle does stand alone in the psalm -- the short-token homography hazard, resolved from the pointed bytes rather than from the raw count. The device_notes doxology claim also checks out: the book-boundary doxologies in the inventory are MT 41.14, 72.18-19, 89.53 and 106.48, none of them in Ps 31, so declining a coda unit_type here is correct and the berakhah at web:Ps.31.21 is the psalm's own praise turn. pmarks_Ps.json holds 0 selah and 0 K/Q verses in Ps 31, so no disclosure or symmetry obligation arises. The closing seam is genuine: web:Ps.31.22 keeps Yahweh as addressee or subject while web:Ps.31.23 turns to a plural congregational imperative, and both out-of-span verses argued in the rejected_alternative are mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs. Two observations. The absence claim carries no digit, which check_universals flags as a lexicon hit; it is true but under-evidenced as written, and the sweep above supplies what it needs. And the rejected_alternative's parenthetical characterising web:Ps.31.19-22 as second- and third-person about Yahweh is exactly right -- it is the row covering web:Ps.31.23-24 that states the opposite over the same four verses, so the cure belongs there and I have filed it there, not here.

The span and its conclusion survive: byte-true אֶֽהֱב֥וּ אֶת יְהוָ֗ה כָּֽל at oshb:Ps.31.24 = web:Ps.31.23 and חִ֭זְקוּ וְיַאֲמֵ֣ץ at oshb:Ps.31.25 = web:Ps.31.24 are plural imperatives addressed to the congregation with Yahweh referred to in the third person, the row closes the psalm without crossing a psalm boundary, and declining a coda unit_type is right since Ps 31 is not one of the four book seams (inventory: MT 41.14, 72.18-19, 89.53, 106.48). The addressee-shift reading is correct. The problems are all in how it is evidenced: the rejected_alternative universalises over four verses and is wrong on one of them, and the substrate signal breaks two quoting rules at once. None of these move the seam, which is why they are filed at the severities they are rather than against the span.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative universalises second-person address over web:Ps.31.19-22, but 1 of those 4 verses, web:Ps.31.21 = oshb:Ps.31.22, speaks of Yahweh in the third person.
challenges.evidence: Byte-true MT oshb:Ps.31.22: בָּר֥וּךְ יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֥י הִפְלִ֘יא חַסְדּ֥וֹ לִ֝֗י בְּעִ֣יר מָצֽוֹר. הִפְלִ֘יא is third-person singular and חַסְדּ֥וֹ carries a third-person singular suffix; the verse contains 0 second-person forms. WEB agrees: “Praise be to Yahweh, for he has shown me his marvelous loving kindness in a strong city.” (web:Ps.31.21). Dual-cite arithmetic: web 31:21 + 1 = oshb 31:22 (Ps 31 is shift+1). check_universals.py flags the row's 'throughout' in this field, which carries 0 digit-bearing sweeps beside it. The addressee-shift conclusion is unaffected -- the shift at web:Ps.31.22|31.23 is from speaking to or about Yahweh to addressing the congregation -- but as written the warrant asserts a uniformity that one of its own four verses breaks, and the row covering web:Ps.31.19-Ps.31.22 characterises those same verses correctly as second- and third-person, so the two rows disagree across a shared seam and the repair is one edit installed on both.

challenges.claim: Substrate signal 1 carries a curly-quoted English string with 0 web: refs in the same field, and the string differs from the WEB wording by 1 word.
challenges.evidence: check_web_quotes.py flags this field: path observed_substrate_signals[0], quote 'all his saints', refs_nearby empty, issue 'curly quote with NO web: ref in its field' -- the field carries oshb:Ps.31.24 twice and 0 WEB refs, while curly quotes plus an inline web: ref in the same field are mandatory at every layer. The string also departs from WEB by 1 word: “Oh love Yahweh, all you his saints!” (web:Ps.31.23) has 'you', the signal's form drops it. The row's own rationale quotes that WEB sentence correctly, so 2 layers of the same row disagree. The underlying Hebrew יְהוָ֗ה כָּֽל collates at byte tier and is not in question; the cure is to mark the string as a gloss of the Hebrew or to quote WEB verbatim with its ref.

challenges.claim: Quote/gloss span desync: the Hebrew quote runs 2 words while the gloss paired with it renders 3.
challenges.evidence: The row pairs חִ֭זְקוּ וְיַאֲמֵ֣ץ (oshb:Ps.31.25), 2 words, with the gloss “Be strong, and let your heart take courage” (web:Ps.31.24), which renders 3. The phrase 'your heart' renders לְבַבְכֶ֑ם, word 3 of byte-true MT oshb:Ps.31.25 (6 words: חִ֭זְקוּ וְיַאֲמֵ֣ץ לְבַבְכֶ֑ם כָּל הַ֝מְיַחֲלִ֗ים לַיהוָֽה), and the Hebrew quote omits it. Quote spans and their glosses must cover the same span, and the toolkit treats both truncation and expansion-without-recut as regressions, so the cure is to extend the quote to include לְבַבְכֶ֑ם or to re-cut the gloss back to its first 2 units -- not to trim the byte-true Hebrew further. Dual-cite arithmetic is otherwise correct: web 31:24 + 1 = oshb 31:25.
